## Outcome and limits

Independent local verification: 188 offline tests passed; ruff passed; mypy passed with MYPYPATH=src; 31 requirements validated. Synthetic retrieval set: 100 entries (40 expected match, 30 tampering, 30 error). This is not live-model evidence or the fixed semantic corpus. Semantic replay, approved runtime snapshot/model settings and real S1/S2 integration remain pending.

Process exceptions: initial tools/permissions blocked execution; default Python3.9 was incompatible and an isolated Python3.12 environment was used. Stubs/DTOs preceded behavioral tests; functional behavior followed RED runs. A proposed out-of-scope mypy.ini write was denied. Review corrections and all failures are retained below. D5 stage-2 architecture-candidate evidence is not established merely by this S3 build session; existing architecture planning evidence must be reviewed separately.

### 2. Interface contract and read-only data contracts

Owner/wire contract proposal: `analysis` owns the advisory/failure wire definition in `contracts.py` as frozen, dependency-free DTOs plus JSON shapes; `api` passes it as read-only input to policy; no policy imports and no shared mutable objects. **Coordination required before Stage A4/any shared-DTO build**: Mei (S1/policy owner), Buna (Testing Lead) and Shiyi must confirm owner and signatures; if S1 PR #41 lands a conflicting contract, stop and revise this plan.

DTOs (all immutable, `tuple`/`MappingProxyType` style, no final disposition/audit ID):
- `PolicyClause(clause_id, text, category, severity_hint, digest, source_ref)`
- `PolicySnapshot(snapshot_id, revision, status="approved"*synthetic only*, digest, clauses: tuple[PolicyClause,...])`
- `RetrievalQuery(case_id, case_revision, text, snapshot_id, snapshot_revision)`
- `RetrievedClause(clause, lexical_score)`, `RetrievalResult(snapshot_id, snapshot_revision, snapshot_digest, clauses: tuple[RetrievedClause,...])`
- `Citation(clause_id, snapshot_id, snapshot_revision, clause_digest)`
- `AdvisoryResult(verdict: allow|review|violate, severity: low|medium|high, rationale, citations, prompt_version, model_id, contract_version, case_id, case_revision, snapshot_id, snapshot_revision, attempt_id)`
- `Usage(status: reported|unknown, input_tokens: int|None, output_tokens: int|None)`
- `AnalysisFailure(code: provider_unavailable|timeout|invalid_response|grounding_unavailable|context_overflow, detail, attempt_id, case_id, case_revision, snapshot_id, snapshot_revision, identity, usage)`
- `ProviderRequest(attempt_id, serialized_context, max_output_tokens, deadline_remaining_ms, model_id, prompt_version, contract_version)`
- `ProviderResponse(raw_json, usage: Usage)`
- `ContextPackage(sections: tuple[ContextSection,...], total_input_tokens, capsule_digest, clause_ids, revision, snapshot_id)`
- `AnalysisHandoff(outcome, severity_preserved, attempt_id, case_revision, snapshot_id/revision, identity; final_disposition=None, audit_id=None, hold_committed=None)`

Injected read-only ports: `SnapshotSourcePort.load(snapshot_id, revision)`, `RetrieverPort.retrieve(query)`, `TokenizerPort.count_tokens(text)`, `ClockPort.monotonic_ms()`, `ProviderPort.invoke(request)`; provider adapter exposes no tools/file/URL/SQL selection. Proposed signatures: `retrieve(query, *, source, retriever)`, `validate_provenance(result, snapshot)`, `validate_advisory(raw_json, *, supplied_clauses, snapshot, identity)`, `assert_no_privileged_fields(payload)`, `assemble_context(query, retrieval, *, tokenizer, config)`, `compact(package, *, tokenizer, config)`, `inject_capsule(package, capsule)`, `invoke_provider(request, *, provider, clock, config)`, `analyze(query, *, source, retriever, tokenizer, clock, provider, config)`, `project_handoff(outcome, *, identity)`.

`ContextConfig` fields limited to: envelope 8,192; input cap 6,144; compaction trigger 4,608; safety/schema 1,024; output 1,024; reserve 1,024; policy 2,048; content/history 2,048; resumable state 512; delimiters 512; max complete clauses 5; per-call ceiling 20,000 ms; caller-supplied remaining deadline ms; `provider_context_limit_tokens` **required, no default**. No 8-second field, no aggregate cap, no retry count, no appeal/reconsideration flag.

### 3. Approval field, trust anchor and canonical digest

- `PolicySnapshot.approval` is required; missing, `unapproved` or `unknown` yields `grounding_unavailable`. No runtime default to approved; digest verification proves integrity only and never authorizes a snapshot.
- Synthetic fixtures carry an explicit test-only approval record plus a separate fixture manifest trust anchor (`synthetic_approved_for_offline_tests`, file list, expected outcomes). The manifest is test scaffolding, not a content claim or runtime approval.
- Canonical digest proposal for approval: normalize clause text with Unicode NFC and CRLF→LF only, preserve all other characters, UTF-8 encode, and take lowercase-hex SHA-256 prefixed `sha256:` as `clause_digest`. Compute `snapshot_digest` as lowercase-hex SHA-256 over compact UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys and `ensure_ascii=False` of `snapshot_id`, `revision`, `approval.status`, `approval.approval_revision`, `approval.evidence_ref`, and `clauses` sorted by `clause_id`, each containing `clause_id`, `clause_digest`, `category`, `severity_hint`, `source_ref`; text is covered through `clause_digest`. Including approval binds the claim to bytes but does not grant authority.

### 4. Async timeout and fencing

- `invoke_provider` computes `budget_ms = min(config.per_call_cap_ms, request.deadline_remaining_ms)`; if `<= 0`, return `timeout` with zero provider calls.
- Otherwise await `ProviderPort.invoke` via stdlib `asyncio.wait_for(..., budget_ms/1000)`. On timeout, call `provider.cancel(attempt_id)` best-effort and return `AnalysisFailure(code="timeout", usage=Usage("unknown", None, None))`.
- Late completion cannot become a current result: `analyze` accepts a response only when its `AttemptIdentity` matches the current attempt/case revision. Fake async provider records cancellation and late completion; `FakeClock` supports deadline arithmetic only. Real `asyncio.wait_for` with an explicitly approved short test-only budget proves timeout enforcement offline; no new dependency or real provider.

**Snapshot authorization and digests.** Inject a read-only synthetic trusted registry mapping snapshot id + integer revision to an approved canonical digest and approval reference, independent of corpus payload. A payload marker or self-computed hash is never authority. **Deadline, timeout and ports.** `analyze` receives an absolute monotonic deadline from the caller at entry and re-evaluates remaining time after retrieval and context assembly; it never restarts the original budget. Retrieval is a pure local, nonblocking port over in-memory data; if any async retriever is used later it must be bounded by the same deadline. Provider invocation creates a task and awaits `asyncio.wait` with `timeout = min(per_call_cap_ms, remaining_ms)/1000` at a test-only 20 ms value where appropriate; generous assertion tolerance is used, and timing is not production SLO evidence. On timeout, mark the attempt expired before a nonblocking `task.cancel()`; never await cancellation or expose a blocking cancel method. ### 2. Concrete typed DTOs and public signatures

All DTOs are immutable frozen records. Literal aliases: `ApprovalStatus = Literal["approved","unapproved","unknown"]`; `UsageStatus = Literal["reported","unknown"]`; `Verdict = Literal["allow","review","violate"]`; `AdvisorySeverity = Literal["low","medium","high"]`; `KnownSeverity = Literal["low","medium","high","unknown"]`; `FailureCode = Literal["provider_unavailable","timeout","invalid_response","grounding_unavailable","context_overflow"]`; `DomainErrorCode = Literal["missing_approval","invalid_approval_status","approval_reference_mismatch","digest_mismatch","missing_corpus","stale_snapshot","conflicting_metadata"]`; `ContextSectionKind = Literal["identity_schema","safety_capsule","policy_clause","content_history","resumable_state","delimiter"]`; `Role = Literal["initial_review"]`.

Records:
- `ApprovalRecord(status: ApprovalStatus, approver_ref: str, approval_revision: str, evidence_ref: str, approved_at: str)`.
- `TrustAnchor(snapshot_id: str, snapshot_revision: int, approved_canonical_digest: str, approval_reference: str, registry_version: str)`.
- `AttemptIdentity(attempt_id: str, case_id: str, case_revision: int, snapshot_id: str, snapshot_revision: int, prompt_version: str, model_id: str, model_version: str, tokenizer_id: str, contract_version: str, role: Role)`.
- `PolicyClause(clause_id: str, text: str, category: str, severity_hint: AdvisorySeverity, source_ref: str, clause_digest: str)`.
- `PolicySnapshot(snapshot_id: str, revision: int, approval: ApprovalRecord, corpus_digest: str, clauses: tuple[PolicyClause, ...])`.
- `RetrievalQuery(attempt: AttemptIdentity, text: str, snapshot_id: str, snapshot_revision: int, known_severity: KnownSeverity, critical_evidence: tuple[str, ...], history_refs: tuple[str, ...])`.
- `RetrievedClause(clause: PolicyClause, lexical_score: float)`.
- `RetrievalResult(attempt: AttemptIdentity, snapshot_id: str, snapshot_revision: int, corpus_digest: str, clauses: tuple[RetrievedClause, ...])`.
- `Citation(clause_id: str, snapshot_id: str, snapshot_revision: int, clause_digest: str)`.
- `Usage(status: UsageStatus, input_tokens: int | None, output_tokens: int | None, usage_unknown: bool)`; invariant: unknown means both token fields are `None` and `usage_unknown` is `True`; reported means both are nonnegative integers and `usage_unknown` is `False`.
- `AdvisoryResult(attempt: AttemptIdentity, role: Role, verdict: Verdict, severity: AdvisorySeverity, rationale: str, citations: tuple[Citation, ...], prompt_version: str, model_id: str, model_version: str, usage: Usage)`.
- `AnalysisFailure(code: FailureCode, detail: str, attempt: AttemptIdentity, usage: Usage, known_severity: KnownSeverity)`.
- `DomainValidationError(code: DomainErrorCode, detail: str, snapshot_id: str, revision: int)`.
- `ModelWireResponse(verdict: Verdict, severity: AdvisorySeverity, rationale: str, citations: tuple[str, ...])`.
- `ProviderRequest(attempt: AttemptIdentity, serialized_context: str, max_output_tokens: int, deadline_remaining_ms: int)`.
- `ProviderResponse(attempt: AttemptIdentity, raw_json: str, usage: Usage)`.
- `ContextSection(kind: ContextSectionKind, text: str, token_count: int, clause_id: str | None)`.
- `ContextPackage(attempt: AttemptIdentity, sections: tuple[ContextSection, ...], total_input_tokens: int, capsule_version: str, clause_ids: tuple[str, ...], preserved_critical_evidence: tuple[str, ...], preserved_history_refs: tuple[str, ...], case_revision: int)`.
- `TrustedCapsule(version: str, identity_schema: tuple[str, ...], safety_rules: tuple[str, ...], citation_rules: tuple[str, ...])`.
- `ContextConfig(envelope_tokens: int, input_cap_tokens: int, compaction_trigger_tokens: int, safety_schema_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, reserve_tokens: int, policy_tokens: int, content_history_tokens: int, state_tokens: int, delimiter_tokens: int, max_complete_clauses: int, per_call_cap_ms: int, provider_context_limit_tokens: int, test_timeout_ms: int | None)`.
- `AnalysisHandoff(outcome: AdvisoryResult | AnalysisFailure, severity_known: KnownSeverity, severity_advisory: AdvisorySeverity | None, attempt: AttemptIdentity, preserved_critical_evidence: tuple[str, ...], final_disposition: None, audit_id: None, hold_committed: None)`.

Ports: `SnapshotSourcePort.load(snapshot_id: str, revision: int) -> PolicySnapshot | DomainValidationError`; `TrustRegistryPort.lookup(snapshot_id: str, revision: int) -> TrustAnchor | DomainValidationError`; `RetrieverPort.retrieve(query: RetrievalQuery) -> RetrievalResult | AnalysisFailure`; `TokenizerPort.count_tokens(text: str) -> int`; `ClockPort.monotonic_ms() -> int`; `ProviderPort.invoke(request: ProviderRequest) -> Awaitable[ProviderResponse | AnalysisFailure]`. There is no blocking cancel method on the provider port.

Public functions: `load_snapshot(snapshot_id: str, revision: int, source: SnapshotSourcePort) -> PolicySnapshot | DomainValidationError`; `lookup_trust_anchor(snapshot_id: str, revision: int, registry: TrustRegistryPort) -> TrustAnchor | DomainValidationError`; `validate_approval(snapshot: PolicySnapshot, anchor: TrustAnchor) -> PolicySnapshot | DomainValidationError`; `compute_corpus_digest(snapshot: PolicySnapshot) -> str`; `verify_corpus_digest(snapshot: PolicySnapshot, anchor: TrustAnchor) -> PolicySnapshot | DomainValidationError`; `retrieve(query: RetrievalQuery, source: SnapshotSourcePort, registry: TrustRegistryPort, retriever: RetrieverPort) -> RetrievalResult | AnalysisFailure`; `validate_provenance(result: RetrievalResult, snapshot: PolicySnapshot) -> RetrievalResult | AnalysisFailure`; `parse_model_wire(raw_json: str) -> ModelWireResponse | AnalysisFailure`; `assert_no_privileged_fields(payload: Mapping[str, object]) -> AnalysisFailure | None`; `validate_advisory(raw_json: str, supplied_clauses: tuple[PolicyClause, ...], snapshot: PolicySnapshot, attempt: AttemptIdentity) -> AdvisoryResult | AnalysisFailure`; `assemble_context(query: RetrievalQuery, retrieval: RetrievalResult, tokenizer: TokenizerPort, capsule: TrustedCapsule, config: ContextConfig) -> ContextPackage | AnalysisFailure`; `compact_context(package: ContextPackage, tokenizer: TokenizerPort, capsule: TrustedCapsule, config: ContextConfig) -> ContextPackage | AnalysisFailure`; `reinject_capsule(package: ContextPackage, capsule: TrustedCapsule) -> ContextPackage`; `remaining_ms(deadline_ms: int, clock: ClockPort) -> int`; `async invoke_provider(request: ProviderRequest, provider: ProviderPort, config: ContextConfig) -> ProviderResponse | AnalysisFailure`; `async analyze(query: RetrievalQuery, deadline_ms: int, source: SnapshotSourcePort, registry: TrustRegistryPort, retriever: RetrieverPort, tokenizer: TokenizerPort, provider: ProviderPort, capsule: TrustedCapsule, config: ContextConfig) -> AdvisoryResult | AnalysisFailure`; `project_handoff(outcome: AdvisoryResult | AnalysisFailure, attempt: AttemptIdentity, known_severity: KnownSeverity, preserved_evidence: tuple[str, ...]) -> AnalysisHandoff`.

Pure snapshot helpers take no attempt and return `DomainValidationError`; every operation with model/provider/context effects requires `AttemptIdentity`. `Mapping` is from `typing`.

**Model wire strictness.** `parse_model_wire` admits only `verdict`, `severity`, `rationale`, `citations` as clause-ID strings. Any extra field, especially `attempt_id`, `case_revision`, `role`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `prompt_version`, `usage`, `action`, `tool` or privileged metadata, yields `invalid_response`. The adapter enriches `AdvisoryResult` from `AttemptIdentity`, local model configuration and provider-reported `Usage`; model JSON cannot assign identity, authority or revision.

### 3. Snapshot authorization, digest and high-severity rules

`TrustRegistryPort` is a read-only synthetic registry mapping `snapshot_id` plus integer `revision` to `TrustAnchor`. Authorization requires exact registry hit, matching approval reference/status, and corpus digest equality with the anchor. A payload `approved` marker or recomputed self-hash without a matching anchor is insufficient; tampered content is rejected with `digest_mismatch` or `approval_reference_mismatch`. Offline registry is synthetic only; runtime approval pending. Runtime approved policy snapshot digest and analysis corpus digest are distinct pinned values with no equality or shared canonicalization assumed; live mapping agreement remains pending.

Corpus digest proposal: clause digest is lowercase-hex SHA-256, prefixed `sha256:`, over NFC-normalized, CRLF→LF-normalized UTF-8 clause text. Corpus digest is lowercase-hex SHA-256, prefixed `sha256:`, over compact UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys and `ensure_ascii=False`, containing exactly `snapshot_id`, integer `revision`, `approval_status`, `approval_revision`, `approval_reference`, and `clauses` sorted by `clause_id`, each with exactly `clause_id`, `clause_digest`, `category`, `severity_hint`, `source_ref`; text is bound through clause digests.

Trusted prefilter severity is `KnownSeverity`; model output is `AdvisorySeverity`. High known severity cannot be downgraded by provider JSON. Critical evidence, history refs and case revision are immutable in `RetrievalQuery` and must appear in `ContextPackage.preserved_critical_evidence`, `preserved_history_refs` and `case_revision`. Compaction removes whole lower-ranked clauses then nonessential history only; if preservation fails, return `context_overflow` with zero provider calls. Failure paths preserve known severity in `AnalysisFailure` and `AnalysisHandoff`.

### 4. Deadline and provider timeout

`analyze` receives an absolute monotonic `deadline_ms` at entry. Remaining time is recomputed after retrieval and context assembly; no stage restarts the original budget. Retriever is a pure local, no-IO port; any future async retriever must be bounded by the same deadline. Provider call uses `asyncio.wait` on a created task with timeout from `min(config.per_call_cap_ms, remaining_ms)`; if remaining is nonpositive, return `timeout` with zero calls. On expiry, mark the attempt expired before nonblocking `task.cancel()`; never await cancellation or expose a blocking cancel method. A done callback consumes exceptions, discards late results and cleans up tasks. A cancellation-suppressing but yielding provider test uses a test-only 20 ms real async timeout with generous assertion tolerance; timing is not production SLO evidence. Fake clock supports arithmetic only; fake tokenizer is not model accuracy evidence.

### 5. Scope, overlap and tests-first

Exact scope is the file table. Reuse/extend PR41-owned `test/offline/conftest.py` and `src/contentguard/__init__.py` after baseline recheck; never overwrite S1 fixtures. `conftest.py` inserts `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "src"` into `sys.path`; no repository-root insertion, package install, manifest, `pytest.ini` or CI change. No worktree or branch mutations by OpenCode. No policy internals import and no policy file changes. ## PM confirmation — S1/S3 interface compatibility and adapter ownership

@xiaolizi33 — confirming as S1 owner. Scope: this confirms interface compatibility and adapter ownership only. It is **not** approval of the S3 OpenCode execution plan, not approval of `docs/policy/community-policy-v1.md` as a runtime snapshot, and does not close FUN-005/INV-2 integration acceptance. Those remain as recorded in the 2026-11-18 PM sign-off.

### 1. Advisory handoff — agreed

Boundary: S3 keeps its immutable advisory DTO inside `analysis`; the API/S2 adapter projects it into `contentguard.policy.contracts.AdvisoryResult`. S3 must not import `contentguard.policy` (contracts or internals) or call `evaluate`/`evaluate_and_commit`; S1 must not import `contentguard.analysis`.

`AdvisoryResult` is a frozen DTO with exactly these fields (`src/contentguard/policy/contracts.py`):

- `role` — `initial_review` (default) or `reconsideration` (optional, disabled by default)
- `verdict` — `allow | review | violate`
- `severity` — `low | medium | high`
- `rationale` — non-empty
- `citations` — sequence of strings (see §4)
- `prompt_version`, `model_id`, `model_version` — non-empty
- `usage` — see §5

`AdvisoryResult.from_payload()` accepts exactly that key set and rejects unknown keys plus `action` / `outcome` / `enforcement` / `actor` / `privileges` / `tools`. The adapter must project only these nine keys — do not pass the S3 DTO wholesale. Case/revision/attempt identifiers stay outside the DTO: `case_id`/`revision` bind to `CaseSnapshot`/`expected_revision`, and `attempt_id` stays in the API/S3 analysis record (S1 has no attempt field; its replay identity is `ReplayKey(actor_id, idempotency_key)`).

### 2. Failure handoff — agreed; S1 receiving interface

S1 already defines `AnalysisFailure(code: FailureCode, detail: str)` with exactly the five codes you listed and the same string values. `detail` must be non-empty. It carries no verdict/severity/model, no committed hold and no audit id.

Receiving interface (`src/contentguard/policy/engine.py`):

- `PolicyEngine.evaluate(*, case: CaseSnapshot, content_text: str, advisory: AdvisoryResult | AnalysisFailure | None = None, review: ReviewRequest | None = None, decided_at: datetime | None = None) -> PolicyDecision`
- `PolicyEngine.evaluate_and_commit(*, store, case, content_text, advisory=None, review=None, expected_revision: int, replay_key: ReplayKey) -> CommitResult` — the commit path. It loads the case row and its **pinned** snapshot, rebuilds the case from the row, and requires `expected_revision` and `ReplayKey`.

Required fields when handing off a failure:

- `AnalysisFailure(code, detail)`.
- `CaseSnapshot` with `case_id`, `revision >= 1`, `status` (accepted/analyzing for a fresh analysis; held/escalated only with a human review), `content_hash`, `policy_snapshot_id`, `policy_snapshot_digest`.
- Pass the failure as `advisory=AnalysisFailure(...)`. The committed case row will carry `analysis_failure_code` with no advisory verdict/severity/model fields — S1 enforces that mutual exclusion. Do not fabricate a verdict, a hold or an audit id.
- For `evaluate_and_commit`: `expected_revision` equal to the case row's current revision, and the case's `content_hash` / snapshot id / digest equal to the row; otherwise `CONFLICT`.
- `content_text` must be the exact submitted text; S1 re-runs its deterministic prefilter against the pinned snapshot's high-severity terms.

Policy behavior: a failure never yields a verdict. With a high-severity prefilter hit → `ESCALATE` (`RULE-PREFILTER-HIGH`, severity high); otherwise → `HOLD` (`FB-ANALYSIS-<CODE>`); both set `requires_human_review=True`. The `detail` text is not persisted in the decision/audit row — only the code — so keep the human-readable detail in the S3/API evidence record.

Preservation: case revision/content hash/snapshot association are preserved by the `CaseSnapshot` / `expected_revision` preconditions above. High-risk signals are preserved by construction: S1 recomputes the prefilter from `content_text` and the pinned snapshot and takes `effective_severity = max(advisory_severity, prefilter severity)` by explicit rank. S1 does not accept a separate external high-risk flag; if S3 needs to carry one, that is a schema change, not part of this handoff.

### 3. Adapter ownership — API/S2

Agreed: the adapter belongs to the API/S2 orchestration layer, not S3 and not S1. S3 owns the analysis output contract; S1 owns the policy input contract; S2/API owns the conversion and the durable analysis/intake record.

**Mei (@Mei-github) implements the adapter in the S2 session**, under `src/contentguard/api/**`. S2 has not started yet; the adapter lands with that slice. It will not appear in the S3 execution plan, and S3 should not modify S1.

DTO ownership: S1 owns the `AdvisoryResult` / `AnalysisFailure` definitions in `src/contentguard/policy/contracts.py`; S3 owns its analysis DTO; the adapter is the only module that sees both.

### 4. Citations

S1's `citations` is a sequence of opaque strings: `AdvisoryResult` checks only that it is a list/tuple and coerces entries to `str`; S1 does not parse clause IDs, look up the corpus, or persist citations in `PolicyDecision` / `AuditRecord`. The adapter should reject empty/non-string entries; S3 owns the canonical encoding and must validate each citation against the exact clauses supplied and the pinned corpus digest before handoff.

Recommended canonical encoding (S3's choice, but keep it stable): `clause_id@clause_revision#sha256:<clause_digest>`, optionally prefixed with `corpus_id@corpus_revision:`. The adapter passes the strings verbatim and does not split or reformat them. Because S1 does not persist citations in the audit row, durable citation evidence lives in the S3/API analysis record; if audit-level citation evidence is required, that is a schema/ADR change, not an adapter change.

### 5. Usage unknown

`Usage(input_tokens, output_tokens, usage_unknown)`. Unknown is represented by the flag, not by zero:

- provider usage unavailable → `Usage(0, 0, usage_unknown=True)`
- a real zero-usage report → `Usage(0, 0, usage_unknown=False)`
- S1 rejects `usage_unknown=True` with non-zero counts; it does not coerce unknown to zero silently
- pass native JSON numbers/booleans, not strings (`from_payload` uses `bool(...)`, so `"false"` would become `True`)
- local token estimates are not billed usage; keep them separate from these fields

### 6. Policy snapshot ↔ retrieval corpus binding

Correct — do not assume they are identical. S1's `PolicySnapshot` is the enforcement-rule artifact: `(snapshot_id, revision, digest)`, where the digest covers rules/fallback/high-severity terms/builtin reasons — **not clause text**. The retrieval corpus is a separate artifact.

Proposed binding for the execution plan (subject to your/Mei's confirmation; not a ratification of the actual snapshot):

- `PolicyReleaseBinding`: `policy_snapshot_id`, `policy_snapshot_digest`, `corpus_id`, `corpus_revision`, `corpus_digest`, `status`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`.
- Each approved release has one binding; changing either side creates a new binding and requires fresh human approval. Old cases keep their pinned binding.
- The retrieval result carries the binding plus the exact ordered clause set (`clause_id`, `clause_revision`, `text`, `provenance`, `clause_digest`) supplied to the model.
- The adapter checks `case.policy_snapshot_id/digest == binding.policy_snapshot_id/digest`; mismatch → `grounding_unavailable`; never silently re-pin.
- Unit tests use synthetic approved-status fixtures. The actual runtime binding and `docs/policy/community-policy-v1.md` remain human-approval gated; live/runtime acceptance stays pending.

S1's decision/audit rows carry only the policy snapshot id/digest, not the corpus ref. Corpus traceability therefore lives in the S3/API analysis record; audit-level corpus evidence would require a schema extension.

Effective configuration changes affecting model behavior require\n123: semantic evaluation; flag settings must be part of replay identity.\n124: \n125: ### Consequences, failure paths and verification\n126: \n127: Benefits: clear ownership, local atomic commit and deterministic offline fault tests.\n128: Costs: SQLite single-writer limitations and conservative holds when grounding is\n129: unavailable. No production scaling or measured quality/latency/token compliance is claimed. An explicit\n130: revision is required before adding external effects, appeals or an LLM summarizer.\n131: \n132: Fallback contract: retrieval/provenance/context overflow/schema/provider failure →\n133: hold with durable queue and fallback identifier; high severity → escalate; policy\n134: error → no final disposition; audit/queue commit failure → roll back, report failure\n135: or unconfirmed accurately; lost response → reconcile by key before retry; semantic\n136: gate failure → block merge. Existing R-1..R-7 remain applicable; retrieval and token\n137: rows are proposed separately in PR #16; they require review and remain planned\n138: until implementation/evidence lands.\n139: \n140: Acceptance tests to plan with Buna (not implemented or executed evidence): all five\n141: invariants including negative bypasses; injection + forged/stale citations; exact\n142: token boundary/overflow/reinjection; retrieval no-match/error; provider timeout;\n143: duplicate request/lost acknowledgment; audit/queue rollback; competing stale review\n144: requests; flag comparison preserving all invariants. A real provider test is separate\n145: from deterministic offline tests and records the actual model/config version.\n146: \n147: Approval status (2026-11-16): PM/non-author approval and CI green are satisfied.\n148: Still outstanding and tracked: PR #11 baseline reconciliation, requirements/testing\n149: co-signs of the limits and fallback contract, and the governance-owner module-contract\n150: reference alignment (separate human docs PR). No implementation before the\n152: test-plan approval and human-approved OpenCode execution plan; this document does not\n153: itself grant those approvals.\n154: \n155: Reopen ADR if retrieval cannot satisfy the build window, numeric limits fail measured\n156: workload, appeal is adopted, external enforcement is added, database contention is\n157: measured, or the model context limit changes.\n158: \n159: \n160: ### Layered context, assembly, budgets and reinjection\n161: \n162: \n163: Layers, in priority order: (1) identity and output schema; (2) standing safety and\n164: authority constraints; (3) retrieved approved policy clauses with provenance;\n165: (4) current submitted content/history as delimited data; (5) resumable state with\n166: case revision, original decision and prior summaries; (6) current role/task.\n167: Persistent authoritative state always comes from storage, never a model summary.\n168: \n169: Pipeline: load pinned revisions → retrieve → validate provenance → deduplicate\n170: by clause ID/digest → rank → allocate budgets → compact lower-priority material →\n171: reinject immutable safety capsule → assemble explicit data delimiters → recount\n172: complete input → dispatch → validate schema/citations → return advisory result.\n173: Prompt composition does not grant authority; deterministic validation still applies\n174: to schema-valid malicious recommendations.\n175: \n176: Proposed numeric design settings, subject to requirements/testing owner and PM\n177: co-sign (not measured SLO compliance). PM provisionally ratified the envelope,\n178: input cap, compaction trigger and 20-second hard per-call cap in the\n179: [2026-11-16 review](https://github.com/CS5351-Group10/contentguard/pull/15#pullrequestreview-5916924512);\n180: requirements-owner and Testing Lead co-signs remain pending:\n181: \n182: | Setting | Proposed value | Meaning |\n183: |---|---:|---|\n184: | Total invocation context envelope | 8,192 tokens | 6,144 input + 1,024 maximum output + 1,024 reserve |\n185: | Input compaction trigger | >4,608 tokens | 75% of input hard cap; recount after reinjection |\n186: | Input hard cap | 6,144 tokens | Overflow after compaction means no provider call; hold |\n187: | Safety/schema allocation | 1,024 tokens | Immutable and never truncated; includes task envelope |\n188: | Approved policy allocation | 2,048 tokens | At most 5 complete clauses, no mid-clause truncation |\n189: | Content/history allocation | 2,048 tokens | Preserve original evidence separately; no silent content loss |\n190: | Resumable state allocation | 512 tokens | Structured IDs/revisions + bounded summary |\n191: | Delimiter/assembly allowance | 512 tokens | Included in total input count |\n192: | Per-invocation hard deadline | 20 seconds | Absolute ceiling, not the <=10-second end-to-end p95 target; no automatic model retries |\n193: | Default invocation count | 1 | At most one extra explicit reconsideration invocation |\n194: \n195: Use the selected model's tokenizer and count the actual serialized request. Provider\n196: context limits must accommodate this envelope or the adapter fails configuration\n197: validation. Record measured provider usage separately from local estimates, including\n198: unknown usage for failed calls. Limits are ceilings, not per-layer padding targets.\n199: \n200: Compaction first removes duplicate/lowest-ranked clauses (whole clauses), then\n201: nonessential historical turns. Missing/unknown enum/type and\n30: extra privileged action/tool fields invalidate an advisory response.\n31: Across all inbound request DTOs, server-authenticated context is the sole source of\n32: actor identity and privileges. Reject caller-supplied actor/role/privilege claims;\n33: server-enriched internal records may contain these fields. Every state-changing\n34: review and policy commit binds expected case revision and pinned policy snapshot;\n35: mismatches yield conflict with no state change.\n36: \n37: ### Operations and owners\n38: \n39: | Owner / operation | Input → output | Failure/side-effect boundary |\n40: |---|---|---|\n41: | API: submit | Submission → committed result or accurate incomplete state | Invalid input: no model call; key+payload mismatch: conflict |\n42: | Analysis: retrieve | Content + pinned policy snapshot → retrieval result | No usable/provenance-valid match: typed failure; no writes |\n43: | Analysis: analyze | Case + retrieved clauses + role → advisory result/failure | No DB mutation or enforcement; bounded context/deadline |\n44: | Policy: evaluate | Immutable case + validated advisory/failure + optional review → proposed decision | Pure deterministic outcome/reason from full input/state tuple |\n45: | Policy: commit | Proposed decision + expected revision + replay identity → commit result | Atomic state+queue+audit; rollback on any failure |\n46: | Escalation: enqueue (internal) | Case + transaction → queue entry | Idempotent per logical case/revision; commit owned by policy |\n47: | Audit: append (internal) | Decision + transaction → audit ID | Unique logical decision ID; no committed status before transaction commit |\n48: | API: review | Authenticated review + expected revision → commit result | Unauthorized/stale review cannot change state |\n49: | API: lookup | Authorized actor + case/audit ID → filtered record | Unauthorized denied; immutable historical policy references |\n50: \n51: Provider adapter exposes only analysis invocation, never execution tools. Retrieval\n52: adapter reads approved local snapshots only; model output cannot choose arbitrary\n53: filesystem paths, URLs, policy revisions or SQL queries.\n54: \n55: ### REST outline\n56: \n57: | Route | Purpose | Principal outcomes |\n58: |---|---|---|\n59: | POST `/v1/submissions` | Submit text with `Idempotency-Key` | 201 committed new triage; 200 reconciled result; 202 durably pending with no final outcome/audit claim; 409 payload conflict; 422 invalid input; 503 definitive persistence failure |\n60: | GET `/v1/cases/{id}` | Authorized case/reconciliation lookup | 200 known state; 403 denied; 404 unknown |\n61: | GET `/v1/review-queue` | Moderator queue view | 200 list; 403 denied |\n62: | POST `/v1/cases/{id}/reviews` | Request human-reviewed transition with expected revision | 200 committed; 403 unauthorized; 409 stale/conflict; 422 mandatory-rule violation; 503 persistence failure |\n63: | GET `/v1/audits/{id}` | Authorized immutable decision evidence | 200 record; 403 denied; 404 unknown |\n64: \n65: Only return 202 when a durable intake intent exists and can be recovered. A queued\n66: hold/escalate can be a committed triage result even though final disposition is not\n67: complete. Never use a success status to imply confirmed queue placement when the\n68: handoff is uncertain. Internal requests carry authenticated principals; client JSON\n69: cannot self-assert moderator privileges.\n70: Response categories are mutually exclusive: committed (200/201, resolvable audit\n71: ID and outcome); durably pending/unconfirmed (202, intent ID and reconciliation\n72: link, no final outcome or committed audit claim); rejected/failed (4xx/503, no\n73: success claim). If reconciliation cannot prove a durable intent, report unavailable\n74: with the replay key rather than manufacturing a 202 recovery guarantee.\n75: \n76: ### Timing and usage handoff\n77: \n78: Analysis receives attempt identity, pinned case revision and a monotonic deadline.\n79: The hard single-call ceiling is 20 seconds, not an end-to-end SLO. The proposed\n80: earlier 8-second intake-to-analysis cutoff remains pending co-sign; callers pass\n81: the remaining time so a provider call cannot extend that analysis window. Timeout\n82: returns typed failure, never an invented verdict. Late results cannot supersede a\n83: committed hold or current case revision; only policy can authorize a new transition.\n84: \n85: Per-attempt usage distinguishes provider-reported input/output from unknown. Context\n86: capacity (8,192 including reserve) is separate from the provisional <=4,000 combined\n87: logical-request usage target; the aggregate hard request budget is still open.\n88: No automatic retries until the aggregate budget/time/unknown-usage policy is approved.\n89: See [blueprint alignment](../../architecture-blueprint.md#provisional-latency-usage-and-evaluation-alignment).\n90: \n91: ### State, retries and transactions\n92: \n93: States: accepted intent → analyzing → hold/escalate/approve/reject. Hold/escalate may\n94: transition to a permitted final disposition only through current authorized human\n95: review and policy evaluation. Final states remain historical; any future appeal\n96: creates a linked successor, not a rewrite. State changes increment revision.\n97: \n98: Key replay identity by authenticated actor + idempotency key; bind it to payload hash.\n99: Persist intent uniquely before analysis; reserve one worker per intent, so duplicate\n100: delivery polls/reconciles rather than invoking another worker or committing twice.\n101: On restart an abandoned reservation is recovered explicitly; it cannot imply a\n102: finished decision. A policy commit checks expected revision and unique decision ID,\n103: then writes case, queue and audit in a single DB transaction. Repeated commit returns\n104: the same result; opposing commits on one revision yield at most one winner.\n105: Policy owns authorization and the commit operation; audit and escalation own their\n106: respective repositories and expose transaction-enlisted ports. They neither commit\n107: independently nor expose protected mutation routes to API/analysis. This is a\n108: proposed port contract, pending governance-owner reconciliation with the existing\n109: dependency rules before implementation.\n110: No network side effects are allowed inside that transaction or in the MVP effect\n111: model. one clause digest from pinned text (REQ-FUN-005).\"\"\"\n    return \"sha256:\" + hashlib.sha256(text.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef retrieve(\n    query: RetrievalQuery,\n    source: query.snapshot_revision, source)\n    if isinstance(snapshot, object) and not isinstance(snapshot, PolicySnapshot):\n        return fail(str(snapshot.detail))\n    if query.corpus_id != snapshot.corpus_id:\n        return fail(\"corpus id mismatch\")\n    anchor = lookup_trust_anchor(query.corpus_id, query.corpus_revision, registry)\n    if not hasattr(anchor, \"corpus_id\"):\n        return fail(str(anchor.detail))\n    approved = validate_approval(snapshot, anchor)\n    if not hasattr(approved, \"clauses\"):\n        return fail(str(approved.detail))\n    verified = verify_corpus_digest(snapshot, anchor)\n    if not hasattr(verified, \"clauses\"):\n        return fail(str(verified.detail))\n    try:\n        ranked = retriever.retrieve(query, snapshot.clauses)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        return fail(f\"retriever error: {type(exc).__name__}\")\n    if isinstance(ranked, AnalysisFailure):\n        return ranked\n    if not ranked:\n        return fail(\"no grounded clause available\")\n    seen: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()\n    unique = []\n    for item in ranked:\n        key = (item.clause.clause_id, item.clause.clause_revision)\n        if ## Final review fixes


### Relayed request

Final Codex review found two remaining correctness bugs; fix with failing tests first, within same approved scope. 1 context._config_valid imposes unsupported power-of-two envelope and provider_limit == envelope. Remove arbitrary power-of-two, allow provider context limit >= envelope; require 0<trigger<=input_cap, full input+output+reserve<=envelope and positive fields. Numeric 4608 is offline config not global max for every test instance. Existing tests asserting arbitrary reject must change to genuine envelope violation; preserve relevant coverage, explain actual changes. 2 service.analyze doesn't check known_severity==query.known_severity before retrieval; retrieval.validate_provenance manufactures unknown severity on forged clauses even when query high. Normalize ALL AnalysisFailure results to original attempt and trusted known severity and reject mismatched transport failure identity. Snapshot re-load after approved grounding allows TOCTOU: use the same verified pinned snapshot or reverify second load against anchor and exact original digest before context/validation. canonical clause digest currently raw UTF8 in retrieval but NFC/CRLF normalization in snapshot: share correct normalization helper and reject every metadata mismatch against pinned clause (category,severity_hint,digest, not just text/source). Add negative test tampered metadata, unicode canonical, swapped snapshot on second load, forged retrieval preserving high severity. Tests red then green, full checks MYPYPATH already supplied. Do not expand files outside allowed scopes, no docs/config/commits. Finish concise summary.
